newsitem.title: UK: British farm minister shrugs off BSE court threat.
newsitem.headline: British farm minister shrugs off BSE court threat.

text.p: Britain's agriculture minister on Tuesday shrugged off calls by a member of the European Parliament for legal action against him for failing to cooperate with an inquiry by the parliament into the "mad cow" crisis.
"If they bring legal action of that kind, they will lose it," Hogg told BBC radio in an interview.
Hogg refused to give evidence in person to the Strasbourg parliament's BSE (Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy) Inquiry Committee when it invited him to do so late last year.

Committee chairman Reimer Berger has alleged this was a breach of Britain's legal obligations under EU law and he called for Hogg to be taken to the European Court, according to reports from Strasbourg.
Any move to sue Hogg would be certain to outrage Eurosceptic Conservatives in Britain who say Brussels already has too much power over the 15 sovereign states which form the EU.
But Hogg said Berger's allegation was a misreading of the EU's founding Treaty of Rome.

He said Britain had cooperated with the committee, providing a mountain of written material and despatching senior civil servants, including government chief veterinary officer Keith Meldrum, to give evidence.
"The real question is whether a minister should go and give evidence to such a committee, and I think the answer is "no'. British ministers are accountable to the House of Commons," he said.
The EU has banned British beef exports since last March when scientists announced a likely link between BSE, and its human equivalent, Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease.
British efforts to get the ban lifted have failed despite the slaughter of thousands of British cattle judged most susceptible to BSE.
